A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COLoKe and contain readable text, equations, figures, Tables 1–4, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding content can be reliably matched; pages 2–9 and 14–19 are visually identical.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original prediction and spectral-recovery experiments on synthetic and real datasets. Appendices C–D report measured update statistics and computation times.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments in Section 4 and the update-frequency and runtime results in Appendices C–D, including Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same deep Koopman embedding, multistep loss, conformity score, threshold update, and conditional optimization procedure. The added citation about non-autonomous systems introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Single Attractor, Duffing, Van der Pol, Lorenz, ETTh1, EEG, and CASES-99 under the same tasks. Replacing biology with neuroscience in the introductory motivation does not change evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains ODMD, OEDMD, OnlineAE, and OLoKe as comparators. The offline Koopman comparison in Figure 2b and fixed-budget OLoKe variants in Figure 4 are also unchanged; the new citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same trajectory counts, train/test arrangements, preprocessing, prediction metrics, architectures, initialization budgets, and online training settings. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The threshold-growth check, spectral-recovery analysis, EEG update-budget comparison, and Appendix C analysis of update behavior are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain five random splits for synthetic experiments and the same uncertainty formulas in Appendix B.1. Reporting of standard errors for synthetic averages and temporal standard deviations for real-data errors is unchanged.

E6.justification: Results in Figures 2–4 and Tables 2–4 are unchanged. For example, COLoKe's single-attractor generalization error remains 2.4 × 10^-7 in Table 2, and its EEG runtime remains 3.67 seconds in Table 4.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 3.3, assumptions A1–A3, and Appendix A proof are identical. No mathematical reasoning, formal guarantee, or assumption is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims about conformal-triggered online Koopman learning, adaptive embeddings, predictive efficiency, and a dynamic regret bound. The citation edits do not change these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of predictive performance and adaptive updates remain unchanged. Both identify the unproved validity of assumption A3 as the main theoretical limitation and propose non-autonomous extensions; v2 merely adds a citation to that existing direction.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical implementation details, architectures, optimizer settings, hyperparameters, and data-processing instructions. The hardware disclosure and code/data access links in Section 4 and Appendix B are unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces Hasnain et al. (2020), cited for biology, with Chrétien et al. (2023), cited for neuroscience. The conclusion adds Gao et al. (2025) for non-autonomous systems. These are limited citation changes; the existing Chrétien et al. (2025) entry only receives bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the introductory application example, the conclusion citation, publication text, and bibliography wording. Section order, terminology, and the scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a NeurIPS 2025 conference footer, adjusts first-page spacing, and reflows the conclusion and references. All figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 updates citations and publication formatting while retaining the method, theoretical analysis, experimental evidence, implementation details, and all appendices. These limited contextual edits leave the paper's substantive clarity, reproducibility, evidential support, and stated limitations materially unchanged.
